answer: A collateralized bonding protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to anchor capital in a time-locked deposit contract. To join the sparrow network, a participant submits cryptographic proof of bonded stake to an orchard registry. An attacker must allocate scarce financial liquidity per fabricated identity, making mass duplication economically unviable. However, well-capitalized adversaries can still purchase sufficient bonds to launch coordinated influence attacks.
